# LUMOS Limitations

## Public release boundaries

LUMOS does not authenticate imported host, inspection, permit, procurement, calibration, chain-of-custody, maintenance, or commissioning records. Event hashes are deterministic change-detection aids, not signatures. Modeled costs are assumptions, not quotes. Replacement-ready hosts are not commissioned. Internal release quality is a software-contract audit, not certification. External APIs may be incomplete, delayed, modeled, provisional, or unavailable. Real deployments require local environmental professionals, asset owners, agencies, laboratories, engineers, safety review, legal authorization, and community engagement.

The optimizer is heuristic except where a reduced-instance exact oracle is explicitly labeled. Cross-domain benefit values are normalized planning indices rather than interchangeable physical quantities or monetized health benefits.

---

## Field-campaign limitations

The v2.7 inspection outcomes are deterministic scenario draws, not observed field results. Modeled inspection and reserve costs are editable planning assumptions, not quotations. Reserve eligibility does not guarantee permission, access, safety, power, hydraulic relevance, sampling authority, or future availability. A complete simulated replacement workflow is not a deployment authorization.

## Verified-host review limitations

A `verified` label means only that the imported record says the required fields were reviewed. LUMOS does not authenticate reviewers, agencies, dates, ownership, legal permission, power service, structural safety, environmental compliance, or sampling rights. Local records and professional review remain authoritative.

## Shared

- Census indicators are area-level estimates and must not be interpreted as individual attributes.
- OpenStreetMap completeness varies, and mapped features do not imply permission, power, safety, inlet suitability, or maintenance access.
- Systematic candidates are mathematical siting proxies requiring field verification.
- Browser-scale guardrails coarsen numerical approximation for large regions without changing the core objective.
- BACI-inspired intervention outputs are planning diagnostics, not proof of causal effects.
- LUMOS is not an emergency, clinical, regulatory-compliance, or deployment-authorization service.

## Heat

- Nationwide current Heat fields are numerical weather-model products, not a universally calibrated street-level urban-temperature model.
- Nationwide Heat uncertainty is an acquisition-priority model and is not universally calibrated predictive variance.
- Live conditions and forecast playback do not automatically change frozen research portfolios.

## Air v1.1 preview

- Pollutant values are atmospheric-model outputs and must not be treated as regulatory monitor readings.
- Wind-aligned covariance represents directional correlation, not a full chemical-transport, dispersion, or street-canyon model.
- Road and industrial layers indicate mapped-source proximity, not traffic counts or emissions rates.
- OpenAQ reference locations reduce posterior uncertainty, but v1.1 does not yet fit their observed pollutant values.
- Air has not yet undergone the held-out reconstruction validation available for the NYC Heat case study.

## Air inference limitations

- OpenAQ coverage, timestamp recency, instruments, and reporting practices vary by location and pollutant.
- Latest values may not be synchronized across monitors and do not guarantee complete time-series coverage.
- Gas conversion from ppm or ppb uses a documented standard reference condition and is an approximation when local temperature and pressure differ.
- The Open-Meteo/CAMS prior remains a coarse atmospheric-composition screening field.
- Wind-aligned covariance is not a chemical-transport, dispersion, or street-canyon model.
- Held-out validation is shown only when enough compatible reference readings are available and is diagnostic rather than regulatory certification.

## Air public-release limitations

The Air public release is a monitoring-design and screening tool. The atmospheric prior is too coarse for street-level regulatory conclusions. OpenAQ coverage may be sparse or temporally inconsistent. Source proximity is not an emissions inventory, and wind-aware covariance is a statistical transport approximation rather than a full chemical transport model. Candidate locations require permission, power, communications, calibration, and field inspection.

## Soil inference preview limitations

- SSURGO map units can contain multiple components and substantial within-unit variability.
- Displayed property values are depth- and component-weighted survey estimates, not laboratory measurements at each evaluation point.
- The soil-health composite is a transparent sampling-priority index, not a contamination probability or agronomic prescription.
- Lead, arsenic, and cadmium concentration fields require compatible local laboratory observations. Without them, LUMOS shows only an explicitly labeled screening-priority proxy.
- Laboratory methods, sample support, depth, date, detection limits, QA flags, and reporting units can differ and must be audited before combining observations.
- Posterior concentrations and intervals are spatial-model estimates, not regulatory exceedance determinations or substitutes for certified sampling and analysis.
- Pesticides, PFAS, pathogens, and unconfigured analytes remain unsupported.
- OpenStreetMap sites are possible sampling or host proxies and do not establish access, ownership, safety, or permission.
- If USDA Soil Data Access is unavailable, LUMOS labels the fallback as low confidence and increases uncertainty; fallback outputs must not be presented as SSURGO findings.


## Soil v1.7 public-release limitations

Import QA can detect many structural problems but cannot certify laboratory methods, chain of custody, sampling design, digestion procedure, geolocation accuracy, or comparability across laboratories. Half-detection-limit substitution for censored observations is a transparent modeling convention with known limitations. Broad plausibility filters are not regulatory thresholds. The four-case evidence suite uses simulated observations and cannot support claims about real contamination or intervention effectiveness.

## Water v1.9 public domain

- USGS instantaneous values can be provisional, sparse, or absent for the selected indicator and extent.
- Inverse-distance screening between stations is not a watershed, contaminant-transport, or hydraulic model.
- Principal-axis direction and branch labels are geometric proxies and do not establish verified upstream/downstream routing.
- Distribution mode does not include authoritative pipe topology, pressure zones, water age, asset condition, treatment operations, or service boundaries.
- OpenStreetMap source features may be incomplete and do not represent permitted loads or verified discharge rates.
- Results do not establish potability, regulatory compliance, contaminant exceedance, laboratory comparability, or causal intervention effects.
- Field use requires access, safety, sampling-method, preservation, chain-of-custody, laboratory, and regulatory review.

## Cross-domain budget allocation

The v2.1 allocation layer compares normalized within-domain planning responses, not raw physical measurements, avoided health outcomes, regulatory benefit-cost values, or causal intervention benefits. Its default costs and response curves are illustrative and are not estimated from vendors or local agencies. The allocator chooses domain program sizes, not geographic sites, hardware specifications, staffing plans, or procurement schedules. Pareto labels apply only to the generated profile portfolio. Operational decisions require locally validated costs, domain evidence, community participation, field verification, and separate domain-specific optimization.


The v2.2 sequential layer summarizes modeled workspaces, not realized causal outcomes. Evidence strength is a reproducible support index rather than a probability that a model is correct. Residual need and realized yield are normalized within domains and cannot be read as comparable physical harm, health burden, or monetary return. Multiple saved workspaces may reflect overlapping areas or repeated analyses; users must review existing-unit counts and evidence independence. Controlled example evidence is synthetic. Operational reallocation requires observed field data, locally validated costs, governance, community participation, domain experts, and independent review.


## Multi-round simulation limitations

The v2.3 trajectory model is deterministic and assumption-driven. Domain learning rates and residual-response coefficients have not been estimated as universal empirical constants. Conservative, central, and upper scenarios do not represent statistical confidence intervals. Simulated reductions in residual need are not forecasts of environmental improvement, sensor performance, regulatory compliance, or health benefit. Long-horizon results can compound assumption error; operational use requires recalibration after every observed round.

## Robust-policy ensemble limitations

The v2.4 ensemble uses seeded planning draws, not empirically calibrated probabilities. Cost multipliers, failure sensitivities, environmental-condition multipliers, and cross-domain correlations are editable assumptions. Conservative, central, and optimistic anchor interpolation does not re-optimize every decision after every random draw. Feasibility probability is therefore an internal scenario frequency, not a guarantee or statistical confidence level. Robust, expected-value, minimax-regret, and most-feasible labels should be recalibrated with local procurement histories, failure records, environmental scenarios, and observed evidence-response data before operational use.

## Spatially coupled deployment limitations

The v2.5 host pool is controlled and synthetic. Distance and category compatibility cannot establish ownership, permission, public access, power, communications, maintenance access, structural capacity, excavation safety, sampling rights, hydraulic connectivity, or environmental compliance. Modeled co-location savings omit procurement quotations, engineering design, construction, laboratory processing, permitting, labor, replacement, and many operating costs. Co-location can also create common-mode failure and correlated missingness. The displayed failure-correlation values are transparent assumptions rather than observed probabilities. Final deployment requires verified local hosts, domain specialists, engineering and safety review, community consultation, and site-specific approval.

## v2.8 live outcome limitations

The event hash chain is deterministic but not cryptographically authenticated. Imported reviewer names, timestamps, permissions, safety findings, and other status fields are accepted as supplied. LUMOS does not verify evidence provenance, legal authority, signatures, property rights, or deployment readiness. A recomputed operational network is not an authorization to install or sample.
